original_clause: Conventions, Weyl duality, FH=HF, FK=-KF, F^2=J; sparse O(N) application of H.
proof_binding: Direct matrix multiplication exchanges T and V. H is a cyclic tridiagonal real symmetric matrix.
qualification: The normalized negative-sign complex Fourier convention is retained. Known Harper structure is attributed, not promoted to historical novelty.

original_clause: A nonexceptional shifted cyclic-tridiagonal resolvent applies in O(N) arithmetic.
proof_binding: A path tridiagonal system plus rank-two corner correction admits linear arithmetic under the stated solver regularity conditions.
qualification: A nonsingular shifted operator and valid solver/pivoting/regularity handling are required. This is not a blanket stability, bit-cost, or FFT runtime statement.

original_clause: Exactly two zero modes, one in each reflection parity, for every N=4m>=4.
proof_binding: Parity block dimensions are 2m+1 and 2m-1. Nonzero Jacobi off-diagonals give simple spectra; signed reversal anticommutes with each odd-dimensional block, forcing one and only one zero eigenvalue per block.
qualification: Includes N=4. No genericity or finite-size extrapolation is needed.

original_clause: F is not any scalar spectral function f(H), including a rational function with invertible denominator.
proof_binding: F preserves both zero lines, with squares +1 and -1; their Fourier eigenvalues cannot agree. A scalar f(H) is scalar on the whole zero eigenspace.
qualification: One commuting Harper operator only. Does not rule out noncommuting operators, products of Green sums, or a larger functional calculus.

original_clause: Unique parity-resolved interpolants and their exact degrees N/2 and N/2-2.
proof_binding: Simple sector spectra and commutation give unique interpolation below block dimension. Endpoint bandwidth/path-distance zeros force both degree upper bounds to be attained.
qualification: Complex theorem for every positive multiple of four N>=4. Degree-zero odd block at N=4 is explicitly included.

original_clause: Leading coefficients 1/(2 sqrt(N)) and -2i sin(2 pi/N)/sqrt(N).
proof_binding: The even endpoint has exactly two shortest unit-weight cycle paths. The odd endpoint has a unique unit-weight Jacobi path and nonzero Fourier entry of the displayed negative-sign convention.
qualification: Changing Fourier sign or scaling H changes the formula. This statement is not the Harper secular polynomial.

original_clause: Direct sparse Horner evaluation is quadratic; degree is not a general arithmetic-circuit lower bound.
proof_binding: There are Theta(N) sparse applications of H, each taking O(N) work in this direct evaluator. Degree alone does not control alternate shared or noncommuting arithmetic implementations.
qualification: No new lower bound on every evaluator, arbitrary Green circuit, or integer multiplication is asserted.

original_clause: Exact finite Harper controls support the symbolic theorem.
proof_binding: The prior direct audit records all-entry exact reconstruction at eleven lengths, using unnormalized W to avoid square-root convention ambiguity; the restored binding records exact canonical theorem identity.
qualification: These are inherited independent computations. No archived implementation or full matrix certificate was rerun here; the all-N conclusion rests on the proof.

original_clause: A real orthogonal Fourier basis gives one four-phase mask.
proof_binding: For complex symmetric unitary F, real and imaginary parts are commuting real symmetric matrices. Real simultaneous diagonalization and F^4=I give phases in {1,-1,i,-i}. Simple-spectrum parity Harper eigenvectors provide a concrete basis.
qualification: Algebraic existence only. The outer real basis can be dense with growing coefficient field and has no supplied fast evaluator.

original_clause: If that basis uses g two-coordinate orthogonal gates, g >= (N/4) log_2 N.
proof_binding: The pair O and O^T uses 2g pair-unitary gates. The free diagonal phase mask leaves matrix entropy unchanged; each pair gate changes entropy by at most two while Fourier entropy is N log_2 N.
qualification: Inherited Ailon pair-unitary entropy framework. Not a lower bound for arbitrary nonunitary Green/shared circuits.

original_clause: The joint commutant of T,V is span{I,J} for every even N>=4.
proof_binding: V has distinct entries within each parity block; T irreducibility makes same-parity diagonal commutants scalar. The unmatched even endpoint forces the first cross-parity coefficient to zero, and recurrence forces the rest to zero.
qualification: No extra invertibility assumption on a candidate M. The original even-N range is broader than the zero-mode theorem and is retained.

original_clause: Both sparse intertwiners characterize M=F(aI+bJ); the full e1 column calibrates M=F.
proof_binding: F^{-1}M commutes with both T,V. Calibration gives (a-1)e1+b e_{N-1}=0, so a=1,b=0 for N>=4.
qualification: One scalar entry is insufficient, and e0 cannot distinguish F from FJ. This is a symbolic certificate, not a fast black-box equality test.

original_clause: Fixed A,B middle-monomial covariance implies diagonal/cycle invariant agreement; mismatch excludes every Q,P for those fixed factors.
proof_binding: For M=A(QP)B, Weyl covariance becomes U(QP)=(QP)V. Diagonal gauges cancel on directed cycle products; permutation only relabels vertices.
qualification: A,B,Q are invertible. Agreement is necessary only. It neither proves Fourier covariance nor supplies calibration, and fixed factors cannot become an all-parameter family claim.

original_clause: For a prescribed permutation, diagonal-gauge existence is exactly a graph-potential consistency problem.
proof_binding: After permutation relabeling, equal support and self-loop values plus consistency on all underlying closed walks (allowing reciprocal traversal) are necessary and sufficient for nonzero componentwise vertex potentials.
qualification: Tests must include all relevant walks and every equation. Dense matrix formation/inversion and entry verification are charged; graph recovery alone is not the whole cost.

original_clause: Four fixed Green-stage examples are rejected by both invariants and have good-reduction characteristic-zero nonvanishing lifts.
proof_binding: The prior independent audit reconstructs the four stage specifications, verifies modular inverses, records diagonal second-moment mismatches, and explains the valid cyclotomic reduction.
qualification: Inherited fixed-instance controls only; no fresh replay here. Modular nonzero witnesses lift only at good reduction with nonvanishing denominators. Modular agreement does not prove a complex identity.

original_clause: Stage applications are linear arithmetic under their solver hypotheses; dense audit inversions are offline work.
proof_binding: Each displayed stage is a bounded sum of tridiagonal solves and diagonal/permutation operations, while formation of full conjugated matrices can require dense work.
qualification: No general fast FFT, stability guarantee, or free preprocessing is inferred. Actual solver guards and paid offline work remain in scope.

original_clause: The owner row additionally includes fixed-stage simultaneous dual-gauge equations from Phase19.
proof_binding: Substituting M=ACB gives U_T C=C W_T and U_V C=C W_V. One common P and one common Q must satisfy both systems. Support/self-loops and all common-ratio closed-walk constraints characterize a fixed P.
qualification: Signature mismatch rejects; a signature match alone never accepts. Ambiguous permutation search hitting a cap is inconclusive. This does not add the unrelated Phase19 norm/conditioning or sandwich theorems to M-HARPER.

qualification: A future constructor, uniform Fourier evaluator, unrestricted no-go, sub-N-log-N FFT, and multiplication improvement are excluded conclusions, not unmet premises of the accepted owner.
